title: Summit and Horizon
premise: Ada Eriksen, a riverboat captain haunted by the drowning of his brother a decade ago, is hired by a desperate government clerk to find a vanished survey team before a ruthless salvage fleet claims their equipment—and the mineral survey that could condemn or save every river town downstream. Racing six tides upriver with an unlikely crew of strays, Ada discovers the team didn't vanish: they found something in the flooded canyon worth killing for, and one survivor has been hiding ever since. When the salvage fleet's sabotage strands them all at the wreck, Ada must choose between salvaging his own redemption and saving people who have become his family. In the end he trades the survey itself to the river—sinking it beyond all reach—and brings his crew home alive, having finally learned that some inheritances are meant to be let go.
about_author: Vesper Okafor spent three years working deckhand jobs on inland waterways before turning to writing full-time. Their fiction draws on oral histories collected from river communities across three continents.

chapters.title: The Sandbar's Mood
chapters.summary: Ada pilots his aging riverboat through fog, reading the water like scripture while dodging debt collectors at every landing. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: weary competence masking grief—he measures life in miles because years hold nothing but his brother's drowning.

chapters.title: A Clerk with Empty Pockets
chapters.summary: Government clerk Miriam Sato hires Ada with coin she barely has, explaining the survey team vanished leaving gear and no tracks. The salvage fleet of Corvo Vane is already moving. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity; the money is too good and too strange to refuse.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Ada assembles a crew of strays: engineer Toma, runaway deckhand Junie, and old pilot Ruth who knows the upper gorge. They load and cast off against the tide schedule. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: fragile hope—the boat feels less empty with strangers aboard.

chapters.title: What the Gear Said
chapters.summary: At the abandoned campsite, Ada reads the left-behind instruments: readings stopped mid-entry, boots gone but coats remaining. Someone left deliberately, upstream, in bare feet. POV: Miriam. Emotional beat: her guilt surfaces—she suspects the survey found something the government wants buried.

chapters.title: Vane's Wake
chapters.summary: Corvo Vane's iron salvage steamer overtakes them; its captain offers Ada triple pay to turn back, then a threat. Ada refuses. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: defiance kindled—refusing Vane feels like refusing his own cowardice from ten years ago.

chapters.title: Junie's River
chapters.summary: Junie reveals she stowed away from a mining town the survey was meant to condemn; her whole village's fate rides on those papers. POV: Junie. Emotional beat: raw fear becoming trust as Ada promises nothing but doesn't turn around.

chapters.title: The Gorge Gate
chapters.summary: Ruth pilots them through the treacherous gorge narrows at night, a passage she alone remembers from before the flood. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into pride; the old woman proves the river still belongs to those who listen.

chapters.title: Bare Footprints
chapters.summary: They find a second camp: signs of the survey team splitting apart, a fight, blood on stone. One set of tracks leads into the flooded canyon caves. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve—they are close, and so is whoever hunted the team.

chapters.title: Tide Against Them
chapters.summary: Vane's crew dynamites a bluff upstream, raising the river to break Ada's tide window. Two days become one. POV: Toma. Emotional beat: fury and ingenuity—Toma rigs the engine past safe limits, gambling the boat's heart for time.

chapters.title: The Survivor
chapters.summary: In a cave above the waterline they find Dr. Ilsa Brandt, half-starved, guarding a sealed case. She reveals the survey mapped a rich vein beneath the towns—and that her own team sold out to Vane before turning on each other. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: paranoid exhaustion cracking into desperate alliance.

chapters.title: What the Case Holds
chapters.summary: Miriam confesses her agency sent the survey to bury the findings, not publish them; the case holds proof both of the vein and of Vane's bribes. POV: Miriam. Emotional beat: shame transformed into purpose—she chooses the towns over her career.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Landing
chapters.summary: Vane's men board at a fueling stop; a brutal close-quarters fight leaves the boat holed and Junie wounded. They drive the attackers off but lose their lead. POV: Junie. Emotional beat: pain and fury—her first real taste of what survival costs, and she pays it anyway.

chapters.title: The Wreck Below
chapters.summary: They reach the drowned canyon where the survey's baseboat sank. Diving in shifts, Ada finds the wreck—and his brother's old ferry, sunk in the same channel ten years ago. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: grief ambushing him at last; the river kept his brother's bones all along.

chapters.title: Brother Water
chapters.summary: Ada dives the ferry wreck alone and recovers his brother's compass, confronting the memory he fled: he was at the wheel when it happened. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: catharsis through near-drowning—he surfaces choosing to live with it rather than outrun it.

chapters.title: Six Hours Short
chapters.summary: The patched hull slows them; Vane's steamer appears on the horizon with the tide turning. Toma proposes running the rapids no pilot has survived. POV: Toma. Emotional beat: terrified exhilaration—the engineer betting everything on his machine and his crew.

chapters.title: The Run
chapters.summary: Ruth calls the lines, Ada steers, and they shoot the rapids in a white-knuckle sequence that nearly kills them all—but puts them ahead of Vane by one tide. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: collective triumph forged in shared mortal risk; the crew becomes a family in the roar of the water.

chapters.title: Vane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Cornered at the confluence, Vane offers a trade: the case for Junie's town spared and everyone's lives. Ada sees the trap but also the truth—any deal with Vane damns someone. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; every choice costs, and he must pick which price to pay.

chapters.title: Betrayal and Fire
chapters.summary: One of Vane's infiltrated crew torches the boat's hold; in the chaos Vane seizes the case and takes Miriam hostage aboard his steamer. POV: Miriam. Emotional beat: despair and clarity—captured, she memorizes the route to Vane's rendezvous with his buyers.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Under cover of night fog, Ada's crew boards Vane's steamer to take back the case and Miriam—a tense, quiet fight of hooks and knives in the dark. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: cold courage; he fights not for revenge but because these people are his to protect now.

chapters.title: Give It to the River
chapters.summary: With Vane beaten and buyers incoming, Ada realizes keeping the survey only moves the war downstream. He sinks the case in the deepest channel where no fleet can follow, letting the river keep its secret. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: costly peace—survival means knowing what to surrender.

chapters.title: Tide's End
chapters.summary: Vane, exposed by Miriam's testimony, flees; the towns stay uncondemned, their fate returned to their own hands. The crew repairs the boat together. POV: Junie. Emotional beat: quiet joy—found family settling into shared work, wounds becoming stories.

chapters.title: Horizon Line
chapters.summary: Ada buries his brother's compass at the gorge gate and casts off with his crew toward new charters, no longer measuring life in miles escaped but in miles chosen. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: earned hope—the inheritance he carries now is the crew, the boat, and the river's mercy.
